data.body: Stopped after genuine plan-review FAIL following one findings-driven description revision. Latest blocking finding verbatim: The rule fires on every cross-artifact read_bytes()/read_text() equality comparison regardless of whether the artifact actually embeds a timestamp, but the only escape is freezing _now_iso/utc_now_iso — which is unavailable for tests comparing timestamp-free artifacts — and a new suppression marker is explicitly out of scope. The plan does not estimate this false-positive surface, yet the lint runs in make verify. Suggested fix: Add a quick survey of current read_bytes()/read_text() equality asserts under tests/** to the plan (count + whether each embeds a clock seam), and either confirm all newly-flagged cases genuinely embed timestamps or reconsider allowing a minimal inline suppression comment for proven timestamp-free comparisons. Advisory also requested defining receiver identity/tracking scope.
